subject: crtf-d
title: CRTF.D.------ALT.F.
description: Diagram in CMOA(II)-34 (Creative Music Outside of America, Level One — France/Italy/Northern Europe/Japan), first of two on book p276. Closes Braxton's Japan analysis where 'the present reality of Japanese creativity is not available for international scrutiny.' (C)CRTF-D (the concept of creative-dynamic) is crossed with ALT-F (alternative functionalism): the question is what creative-dynamic produces when crossed with alternative-functionalism under conditions of the Japan-West one-way culture gap. PROG-CONT (progressional continuance) and POL-DY (political dynamics) form the upper-center cluster. (P)CULT-INFO-DY (point-of-activation culture-information dynamics) anchors the upper-right output via a long bridge from the central axis. ALT-F itself sits centrally below. PROJ-CONT (projectional continuance) and LK-IMP (linkage implication) form the right-side outputs. INFO-DS (information descent), DYM-F (dynamics fundamentals), and STF (source-transfer functionalism) form the lower upstream cluster. Structural argument: creative-dynamic-as-concept crossed with alternative-functionalism is mediated by alternative-functionalism itself as central hub (an unusual but structurally telling configuration where the partner doubles as the hub). The (p) prefix on culture-information-dynamics is load-bearing — Japanese culture-information operates at point-of-activation rather than as sustained system, exposing Braxton's diagnostic that Japanese creative-dynamic only triggers culture-information event-by-event because the Western recognition apparatus does not provide sustained channels. The triple lower upstream (information-descent, dynamics-fundamentals, source-transfer-functionalism) gives the schematic its decentralization, but the productive outputs depend on the conditional point-of-activation hub firing.
